claim: FLUE (AAAI 2025) sets zero additional inference cost as one of two 'ideal' criteria for LLM uncertainty estimation, achieving token-level Monte Carlo samples from a single forward pass by converting parameter redundancy into randomness.
stance_target: what AAAI reviewers reward in UQ-for-LLM papers
quoted_support: An ideal uncertainty estimation for LLMs should meet two criteria: 1) incur no additional inference cost and 2) capture the semantic dependencies of token-level uncertainty within sequences.

claim: FLUE demonstrates competitive uncertainty-estimation performance in open-ended QA without adding extra inference overhead versus multi-sample uncertainty baselines.
stance_target: inference-cost tradeoff bar for confidence/uncertainty methods at AAAI
scope_conditions: open-ended question-answering tasks only, not code
quoted_support: we demonstrate that FLUE can achieve competitive performance in estimating the uncertainty of generated sentences without adding extra inference overhead.

claim: FLUE was published in the AAAI Technical Track on Machine Learning II, AAAI-25 Vol. 39 No. 16, confirming AAAI main-track (not workshop) status.
stance_target: venue classification of FLUE as AAAI main-track precedent
quoted_support: Issue Vol. 39 No. 16: AAAI-25 Technical Tracks 16 Section AAAI Technical Track on Machine Learning II

claim: FLUE requires learning a separate post-processing model of state transitions from token-level to sequence-level uncertainty, adding methodological machinery beyond raw sampling.
stance_target: comparison of UQ method complexity vs DPRC's simpler tokenized-Brier digit readout
quoted_support: we theoretically analyze the FLUE sampling method and employ a post-processing method to learn the state transitions from token uncertainty to sequence uncertainty.
